purpose: Full-bank production-marker regression on all school-mock-tagged Physics, Chemistry and Year 1 Pure Maths flashcards, keeping original IDs/progress, correct/wrong variants, and a length heuristic distinguishing flashcards from long answers.
notes: 21 everyday non-answer variants, including straight/curly apostrophes, must score wrong on each of the 3,382 mock-tagged cards (71,022 negative probes).

Prior to changing production normalisation, independently checked 12,550 original unpatched model/accepted/rejected examples across the core and all 56 supplement files with zero altered authored outcomes.
Additional adversarial regression: prefix each complete correct model answer with 'not' and require a wrong mark, including all 3,382 school-mock-tagged cards.
Tests actual production answer evaluator and applies all patch functions up to v332 to original deck.
Explicit accepted/rejected lists are test fixtures; correct responses never seen before may still need human calibration.
Length thresholds are simple regression alarms, not proof that every card is semantically well written.
Original multi-mark exam questions remain in separate practice banks; never force them into flashcards.
Full AQA bullet-level coverage certification and open-ended unseen-answer review remain unfinished.
fix: The original tera (T) card falsely accepted 'I don't know', 'I can't remember' and 'I can't recall' because text normalisation split contractions at an apostrophe, producing an irrelevant standalone t token. v334 preserves apostrophe-containing words during normalisation, and uses a narrow non-answer guard for 21 complete hesitation phrases. The legitimate 'T' and 'tera' answers remain accepted.
